sources.entry: ray - A unified framework for scaling AI and Python applications.

summary.one_liner: Ray is a unified Python framework for scaling AI and Python applications from a laptop to a cluster, with a core distributed runtime and a set of AI libraries.
summary.what_it_does: Ray provides a core distributed runtime built around three abstractions: tasks (stateless functions run in the cluster), actors (stateful worker processes), and objects (immutable values shared across the cluster). On top of that it offers AI libraries named in the README: Data (scalable datasets for ML), Train (distributed training), Tune (hyperparameter tuning), RLlib (reinforcement learning), and Serve (scalable, programmable serving). The README says the same Python code can be scaled from a laptop to a cluster, and that Ray runs on any machine, cluster, cloud provider, and Kubernetes. It includes a Ray Dashboard for monitoring and a Ray Distributed Debugger for debugging. Install with pip install ray.
use_cases: scale Python code from laptop to cluster
notable: Unified framework covering both general Python task scaling (Ray Core) and AI libraries (Data, Train, Tune, RLlib, Serve)
Core abstractions: tasks, actors, and objects
Ray Dashboard and Ray Distributed Debugger for monitoring and debugging
Runs on any machine, cluster, cloud provider, and Kubernetes per the README
caveats: README does not state license terms in the text provided; license is not named in the README excerpt
Nightly wheels and detailed installation require the external Installation page
